searchText: This is the best way for now (afaik). Local change in EELS. Fill with new change in EEST. It will be easier in the near future! cc <@547171287831805972> <@830368514225340436> - if there is a better way 😄 (i usually push to git branches, change eels resolutions to the git branch, so not the best way :P) I'm not sure how you're overriding, but I've found it convenient to do this (`fish` syntax): ```console set -x EELS_RESOLUTIONS '{"Osaka": {"path": "/home/path/to/execution-specs/"}}' ``` As <@755913785620824175> mentioned, this should get easier soon. We plan to move the `./tests` directory from `execution-spec-tests` to `execution-specs` so that spec and test implementers need only concern themselves with one repo & branch . <@735470118577897474> did you manage to run coverage (against EELS) at all? Never really found out how... apparently I could add `--cov` to `uv run fill` but did not seem to do much Yeah, that would be the way, but because the EELS implementation (branch) is "resolved" via the `ethereum-spec-evm-resolver`, `coverage.py`/`pytest-cov` can't track the EELS source. I think I hacked it once, but I'm not sure. Let me ask a friend and get back to you later. Actually, <@830368514225340436> is that/my friend, you once generated coverage of EELS against EEST, right? How did you do it? This will also be solved by moving ./tests to execution-specs btw. Seems like 99% of all problems can be solved by moving `./tests` to `execution-specs` Thank you for the info though Yup, it's time to clean up this historical tech debt. Would you mind sharing what you're using EELS/EEST for? No obligation. I am (attempting) to write an implementation of [EIP-7932](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7932) I have been told it makes life easier for client teams, instead of just going "Here is a problem, it is your problem now." It certainly makes it easier to assess the required effort if an EELS implementation and (basic) tests are available. This helps when deciding whether it's included in a fork, or not. I understand it requires some effort though. That coverage report was generated by running the json fixtures against EELS Makese sense. Do you have a command for EELS to do that? Update this [line](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-specs/blob/e33bb9a8b4b6a4898bd19f731685e38c366817cc/tests/helpers/__init__.py#L26) to point to the appropriate json fixtures containing all the tests you want to run. Then ``` pytest -m "not slow" -n auto --maxprocesses 10 --cov-config=pyproject.toml --cov=ethereum --cov-report=term --cov-report "xml:coverage.xml" --no-cov-on-fail --cov-branch --ignore-glob='tests/fixtures/*' ``` cc <@735470118577897474> Thank you, this makes my life significantly easier.

excerpts.author: danceratopz
excerpts.content:
I'm not sure how you're overriding, but I've found it convenient to do this (`fish` syntax):
```console
set -x EELS_RESOLUTIONS '{"Osaka": {"path": "/home/path/to/execution-specs/"}}'
```

excerpts.author: danceratopz
excerpts.content: As <@755913785620824175> mentioned, this should get easier soon. We plan to move the `./tests` directory from `execution-spec-tests` to `execution-specs` so that spec and test implementers need only concern themselves with one repo & branch .

excerpts.author: gurukamath
excerpts.content:
Update this [line](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-specs/blob/e33bb9a8b4b6a4898bd19f731685e38c366817cc/tests/helpers/__init__.py#L26) to point to the appropriate json fixtures containing all the tests you want to run.

Then
```
pytest -m "not slow" -n auto --maxprocesses 10 --cov-config=pyproject.toml --cov=ethereum --cov-report=term --cov-report "xml:coverage.xml" --no-cov-on-fail --cov-branch --ignore-glob='tests/fixtures/*'
```

excerpts.content: Thank you, this makes my life significantly easier.
